title: Interpret a rare positive alarm
scope: One binary observation with specified sensitivity and false-positive rate

items.prompt: A population has fault prevalence 1%. Sensitivity is 90%; the false-positive rate on nonfaulty cases is 5%. Given ONE positive result, compute P(fault | positive), as a probability, not a percentage.
items.solution: Use p·0.9/[p·0.9+(1−p)·0.05]=2/13. A count table gives the same ratio; sensitivity alone is not the posterior.

items.prompt: Among 10000 parts, prevalence is 2%. One screening test has sensitivity 80% and false-positive rate 2%. The expected-count table has 160 positive defective parts and 196 positive nondefective parts. Given one positive, compute P(defective | positive) as a probability. Tolerance ±0.001 for numeric fields; follow the stated units.
items.solution: Condition on the positive column: TP/(TP+FP)=160/(160+196)=0.449438202247191. Do not divide by all parts or by the prevalence alone.
